# nixarchy.pkg

> A menu for changing what is installed on a NixOS machine running nixarchy.
> It searches nixpkgs, turns curated apps and services on and off, sets NixOS
> options with a form built from each option's declared type, and queues the
> result. Nothing is built until the user presses `a`.

## The one thing to get right when answering about this

It manages a SELECTION, not the machine. The packages a user declares in
their own NixOS configuration are not listed here, not counted here and not
removable here. On a machine that adopted nixarchy as a flake input -- which
is most of them -- that means the Selection tab can show one row while the
system has hundreds of packages. This is deliberate: the whole selection
hangs off a single import, so removing nixarchy removes everything it added
and orphans nothing.

The consequence worth warning a user about: if a package is in their own
configuration AND in the selection, removing it here removes it from the
selection and it stays installed. The panel is not lying when it reports the
removal.

## How a change happens

1. The user picks a row. One marked line is written into
   `~/.config/nixarchy/{apps,services,advanced}.nix` -- a file they own.
2. Nothing is built. The footer and the bar widget show a queued count.
3. The user presses `a` (or `SHIFT+A` for a terminal). `nixarchy-apply`
   copies the selection into the flake directory and rebuilds.
4. The result is a NixOS generation, so it can be rolled back.

Every write goes through a writer that ships with nixarchy
(`nixarchy-pkg-add`, `nixarchy-app-enable`, `nixarchy-opt-remove`,
`nixarchy-apply`). The plugin calls them and draws what they report; it does
not predict success.

## Things that are true and easy to get wrong

- An absent `unfree`/`broken` flag is absent EVIDENCE, not a "no". A stale
  index carries no flags at all and every package reads as free.
- An untouched field in the option form writes nothing, on purpose: the value
  shown is the default, and a copied-out default reads like a decision.
- The two nixpkgs channels share no store paths. A package taken from the
  other channel brings its own entire closure -- measured at 1.5 GB for vlc.
- `ESCAPE` during a build stops you watching the log. It does not stop the
  build.
- Options whose type has no one-word answer get a commented scaffold rather
  than a widget. That is the honest outcome, not a missing feature.
